title: Isokinetic Robotic Device to Improve Test-Retest and Inter-Rater Reliability for Stretch Reflex Measurements in Stroke Patients with Spasticity
protocol: Perform the screening process using the following inclusion criteria.
Check for upper extremity hemiparesis due to stroke.
Ensure patients are over the age of 20 years.
Evaluate mild elbow joint spasticity, grading MAS 1-2.
Confirm no previous disease affecting function of the hemiparetic arm, except for stroke.
Verify absence of hemodynamic instability.
Assess no severe elbow contracture.
Check possibility for shoulder abduction to 90° and forearm in neutral position without pain.
Ensure normal cognitive, language, visuospatial, or attention ability to follow experimental procedures.
Recruit subjects after providing a detailed explanation of the entire study and expected clinical issues.
Obtain consent prior to inclusion.
Place a fixation arm on the front part of the robot.
Secure the fixation arm to the desk using clamps.
Attach casters with stoppers to the bottom of the robot.
Use a personal computer as the central control system.
Implement the robot control algorithm using a real-time processor.
Run the data input/output loop at 1 MHz from the FPGA module.
Execute the robot motion control loop at 1 kHz.
Transmit robot data in the communication loop at 250 Hz.
Mount a torque sensor between the manipulandum and the motor to measure reaction force.
Transfer torque data to real-time processor via NI-9237 module.
Process filtered torque data with FPGA module and low-pass filter at 100 Hz.
Measure joint angle using an encoder attached to the motor.
Transfer angle data to the real-time processor via motor driver.
Collect muscle activity data with eight-channel surface EMG device.
Filter EMG data with a bandpass filter (20-450 Hz) and notch filter (60 Hz).
Transfer measured EMG data directly to PC.
Secure both sides of the shoulder and abdomen with seatbelts.
Place the subject’s hemiparetic arm lightly on the robot manipulandum without fastening the strap.
Unfasten the fixation block of the linear slider.
Adjust the height of the robot using the lab jack until the patient’s shoulder is abducted 90°.
Confirm the abduction angle using a goniometer.
Instruct the subject to hold the handle and fasten the hand to the handle with straps.
Align the rotation axis of the robot and anatomical axis of the elbow joint.
Flex and extend the elbow joint so that the position of the cuff can be readjusted naturally in an optimal position without generating resistance during the elbow movement.
Fasten the fixation block to fix the position of the cuff.
Fasten the straps of the forearm cuff.
Attach the surface EMG electrodes on the biceps brachii muscle in the hemiparetic arm.
Input the patient's hemiparetic side information into the program GUI (right or left).
Set the elbow 90° flexed using a goniometer.
Press the 90 deg set button on the GUI panel.
Press the Finish set button on the GUI to switch the robot to the actuating state.
Click the buttons on the Motor run panel on the left side of the GUI in order from top to bottom.
Turn on the Angle set button and set the speed to 1°/s.
Click the run button.
The robot will extend the elbow slowly at 1°/s from a 90° flexed posture until the reaction torque reaches a certain threshold level or extends by 170°.
Change the speed to -1°/s and click the run button again.
The robot flexes the elbow slowly until the reaction torque reaches the threshold level.
Click the Back button on the control panel.
Set the speed to 150°/s.
Turn on the Inertia test button and then the Run button.
Repeat steps of setting the speed, turning on the inertia test button, and running the program two more times.
Determine a proper peak torque value from the measured data.
Enter the peak torque value on the program GUI.
Determine a proper period value from the measured data.
Enter the period value on the program GUI.
Click the Back button on the panel.
Flex the elbow to the minimum angle posture.
Inform the subject and click the Run button.
Extend the patient’s elbow at a rate of 150°/s until reaching the maximum angle or reaction torque threshold level.
Repeat steps for three training operations, taking a 5 min rest after two repetitions.
Click the Back button on the panel.
Flex the elbow to the minimum angle posture.
Click the Run button without informing the subject.
Extend the patient’s elbow at a rate of 150°/s until reaching the maximum angle or reaction torque threshold is reached.
Store time, angle, reaction torque, and trigger signal data during the test.
Take a 2 min break between sets.
Repeat steps for extending the elbow two more times.
Take a 5 min rest after performing three sets.
Click the Back button to flex the elbow to the minimum angle posture.
Click the Free run button to switch robot operation to manual mode.
Hold the handle of the manipulandum and stretch the subject’s arm at a constant speed of 150°/s.
Turn off the Free run mode and take a 2 min break.
Repeat steps for manual stretching two more times.
Take a 10 min rest after completing the whole experiment with the first rater.
Change to the second rater.
Repeat steps from robotic extension to manual stretching.
Process raw EMG data using root mean square (RMS) to smooth the data.
Amplify processed EMG data 50 times.
Synchronize EMG data with robot angle data using trigger signals from each dataset.
Determine AoC manually as the starting point of the RMS EMG upsurge.
Process raw EMG data using the RMS method to smooth the data and amplify it 50x.
Synchronize EMG data and robot angle data using trigger signals of each dataset.
Determine AoC manually as the starting point of the RMS EMG upsurge.
Calculate ROM, maximum velocity, and assessment time from each assessment trial.
Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between AoC based on EMG criteria and torque criteria.
